observed_title: Itô Isomorphisms for Lp-Valued Poisson Stochastic Integrals
version: arXiv:1208.3885v3; published in The Annals of Probability 42(6) (2014), 2595–2643, DOI 10.1214/13-AOP906; electronic reprint, 51 PDF pages.

read_ranges.scope: 全文逐行阅读：Theorems 1.1/1.2，classical Lq proof、all six p/q cases in Appendix B、noncommutative Lq extension and random-matrix intermezzo, decoupling appendix, acknowledgements and references.

topic_relevance.K03: adjacent method source only. It develops moment-norm decompositions and maximal estimates for compensated Poisson stochastic integrals in Lq-valued and noncommutative Lq settings; these can inform construction/checking of increment bounds for a Poisson-indexed process. It contains no pointwise majorizing-measure functional, admissible chaining, or simultaneous all-index envelope.
topic_relevance.J04: adjacent integral-calculus source. It supplies Itô isomorphisms and compensated-Poisson integration estimates under deterministic σ-finite intensity, with an explicit distinction between integrand norms and integral maxima. It does not construct a state-dependent/nonhomogeneous compensator or an exit-settlement/Fubini procedure.

definitions.name: simple adapted Poisson integrand and compensated integral
definitions.statement: For a σ-finite mark space (J,ν), the compensated Poisson random measure has deterministic intensity dt×ν. A simple adapted Lq(S)-valued F is constant on finitely many time/mark rectangles with coefficients measurable at the left endpoint. Its integral is the corresponding finite sum against compensated Poisson increments.

definitions.name: Itô-isomorphism integrand norm
definitions.statement: The space I_{p,q} is a piecewise intersection/sum of the square-function space S_q^p and the two Poisson magnitude spaces D_{q,q}^p,D_{p,q}^p. Which intersections and sums occur depends on the relative positions of p and q with respect to 2; the article states six cases.

definitions.name: vector-valued Rosenthal norm
definitions.statement: For independent mean-zero Lq(S)-valued ξ_i, Theorem 1.2 compares (E||Σ_i ξ_i||_{Lq}^p)^(1/p) with a six-case norm built from S_q,D_{q,q},D_{p,q}; the upper estimate extends to p=1 or q=1 (or both), while the two-sided theorem is for 1<p,q<∞.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1.1 (classical Lq-valued Poisson Itô isomorphism)
assumptions: 1<p,q<∞; (S,Σ,σ) is a measure space and (J,J,ν) is σ-finite.
N is a Poisson random measure with deterministic intensity dt×ν and F is a simple adapted Lq(S)-valued process; t>0 and B∈J.
theorem_cards.statement: (E sup_{0<s≤t} ||∫_(0,s]×B F dN~||_{Lq(S)}^p)^(1/p) ≃_{p,q} ||F·1_(0,t]×B||_{I_{p,q}}, with I_{p,q} given by six explicit p/q-position cases formed from S_q^p, D_{q,q}^p and D_{p,q}^p. The upper estimate ≲_{p,q} remains valid when q=1; the two-sided equivalence is asserted for 1<p,q<∞.
proof_steps: Apply Doob’s maximal inequality to reduce the maximal integral to the terminal integral; for 1<q<∞ use UMD decoupling to replace the adapted integral by the conditionally independent decoupled sum.

For 2≤q≤p, condition on the original environment and apply Theorem 1.2 to the independent mean-zero Poisson increments. Lemma 3.4 controls moments of compensated Poisson variables when rectangle intensity λ≤1; refine the time/mark partition to enforce that condition.

For 1<p≤q≤2, decompose the integrand into three dense elementary pieces corresponding to S_q^p,D_{p,q}^p,D_{q,q}^p, apply conditional expectation onto the partition algebra, bound each decoupled term, and recover the reverse inequality by duality. Appendix B gives the remaining p/q cases. Full proof spans source lines 797–998 and 1931–2088; all regions were read.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Main proof of Theorem 1.1 in the representative exponent regions.
Appendix B: remaining exponent regions and completion of the upper-bound proof; PDF page list stored per line range.

gaps: Constants depend on p and q; no p/q-uniform constants are claimed.
The theorem is for classical Lq(S) and, separately, noncommutative Lq(M); it is not a general theorem for arbitrary Banach-valued integrands.
The stochastic integral extends from simple adapted integrands by closure in I_{p,q}; no mixed-tail generic-chaining conclusion follows directly.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1.2 (Lq-valued Rosenthal inequalities for independent summands)
assumptions: 1<p,q<∞ for the two-sided statement; (ξ_i) is a finite independent mean-zero sequence in Lq(S).
theorem_cards.statement: The Lp(Ω;Lq(S))-norm of Σ_i ξ_i is equivalent, with constants depending only on p,q, to a six-case combination of S_q,D_{q,q},D_{p,q}. The one-sided upper estimate remains valid for p=1 or q=1, including both equal to 1.
proof_steps: Prove the core 2≤p,q case from symmetrization, Khintchine, and a Rosenthal-type maximum of square-function and q-moment terms.

Use duality of intersection/sum spaces for the lower bound and a case-by-case decomposition with conditional expectations for other positions of p,q relative to 2. The full proof is source lines 500–665, PDF pp.12–16.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Complete proof of Theorem 1.2 in the classical Lq setting.

gaps: The proof invokes standard Khintchine, symmetrization, Hoffmann–Jørgensen and scalar Rosenthal inequalities; this reading checked their use in the displayed reductions but did not independently reprove these external inputs.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 7.1 (noncommutative Lq-valued Poisson Itô isomorphism)
assumptions: 1<p,q<∞; M is a semifinite von Neumann algebra with normal semifinite faithful trace; N has deterministic σ-finite intensity; F is a simple adapted Lq(M)-valued process.
theorem_cards.statement: The maximal Poisson integral Lp norm is equivalent, with constants depending on p,q, to I_{p,q} built from row and column square-function spaces plus the D_{q,q}^p,D_{p,q}^p magnitude spaces in six p/q cases.
proof_steps: Use UMD decoupling and Doob maximal inequality. For 2≤q≤p apply the noncommutative Lq Rosenthal inequality pointwise to independent compensated increments; for the opposite low-exponent case decompose into four pieces (column, row, D_{p,q}, D_{q,q}) and use duality. The paper explicitly sketches these representative cases and omits straightforward modifications for others.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Proof sketch of Theorem 7.1, including the representative exponent regimes and duality.

gaps: Several exponent-regime modifications are referred to as straightforward rather than written out.
The result still assumes a Poisson random measure with deterministic intensity and Lq(M) geometry; it does not cover arbitrary Banach spaces.

constant_dependence.explicit: The equivalence constants in Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 7.1 depend only on p,q. Proof constants also pass through the UMD/decoupling and Doob constants; none is claimed uniform over p or q. The finite-n Poisson moment comparison uses constants depending on the moment order when each rectangle intensity is at most one.

endpoint_limits.exponents: Two-sided isomorphisms require 1<p,q<∞. Theorem 1.1 explicitly retains only its upper estimate at q=1; Theorem 1.2 retains its upper estimate at p=1 and/or q=1. No endpoint p=∞ or q=∞ is stated.
endpoint_limits.integrands: Main statements start with simple adapted integrands and extend to the indicated norm closures.
endpoint_limits.intensity: The measure is deterministic and σ-finite; small-rectangle arguments use λ≤1 after refining the partition.

reusable_methods.method: Decouple the Poisson integral into conditionally independent centered increments and apply a vector-valued Rosenthal inequality.
reusable_methods.transfer: Can support finite-increment moment estimates in Lq-valued jump processes after verifying adaptation, UMD/decoupling, and deterministic-intensity assumptions; it supplies no chaining step or all-index theorem.

reusable_methods.method: Represent integrand complexity by the square-function part plus p- and q-moment Poisson magnitude norms, with intersections/sums depending on exponents.
reusable_methods.transfer: Useful for candidate Banach/Poisson increment scale bookkeeping only when the target spaces and p,q regime match; do not infer these six Lq formulas for arbitrary Banach spaces.

unchecked: All 51 extracted PDF pages were read, including Appendix A decoupling, Appendix B remaining exponent cases and references. Theorem 1.1/1.2 formulas were visually checked on PDF pp.3 and 6; the noncommutative theorem on p.41.
